# Agent Concepts

This page explains the agent concepts used by tfctl when interacting with HCP Terraform. Understanding these concepts helps you configure and use tfctl effectively in your infrastructure automation workflows.

## Introduction

Agents are components that facilitate communication between tfctl and HCP Terraform. They handle authentication, request routing, and data transformation, enabling seamless integration between your local environment and HCP Terraform's cloud infrastructure.

## Agent Architecture

An *agent* is a software component that acts as an intermediary between tfctl commands and the HCP Terraform API. Agents manage the following responsibilities:

- Authentication token management and refresh
- Request serialization and deserialization
- Error handling and retry logic
- Connection pooling and resource management

Agents operate transparently to provide a consistent command-line experience while handling the complexity of API interactions.

## Deployment Models

tfctl supports multiple agent deployment models depending on your infrastructure requirements.

### Local Agent

The local agent runs on the same machine as the tfctl CLI. This is the default deployment model and is suitable for:

- Individual developer workflows
- Local testing and development
- CI/CD pipelines with ephemeral runners

### Remote Agent

Remote agents run on dedicated infrastructure and can be shared across multiple tfctl instances. This model is suitable for:

- Enterprise deployments with centralized authentication
- Environments with strict network policies
- High-availability requirements

## Agent Configuration

Agents are configured through tfctl profile settings and environment variables. Configuration options include:

- API endpoint URLs
- Authentication methods
- Timeout and retry settings
- Logging and debugging options

Refer to the [profile commands](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/profile) documentation for details on configuring agent behavior.
